decision: The project is renamed from ChampHLA to PanelHLA.
rationale: The 2026-09-08 amendment demoted Champion-Challenger from the primary method to a retained ablation and promoted equal-weight plurality over a modality-appropriate caller panel.
A name that literally encodes 'Champion' therefore misdescribes the method the paper reports.
PanelHLA names the caller panel, which is the object the paper is actually about.
The rename also resolves a pre-existing split in which the GitHub repository and Nextflow pipeline were named pihla / pihla-publish while the manuscript said ChampHLA.
rename_rule: Rename labels. Never rename an identifier that lives inside data, because doing so either invalidates a checksummed artifact or changes what a run reproduces.

renamed.code_labels: docstrings, CLI --description text, generated table headings, the ENA User-Agent string
renamed.live_decision_exception: decisions/publication_route.json IS renamed, unlike everything else under decisions/. It is a live routing decision describing the current active method, not a record of a past decision, so leaving it naming the old method would make it wrong rather than historical.

deliberately_not_renamed.reason: These are values inside frozen prediction tables and checksummed artifacts. Renaming them would invalidate every artifact and break the freeze chain.
A seed is an input, not a label. Changing the string changes which subjects a roster selects, so the frozen rosters would no longer reproduce.
Version identifiers embedded in checksummed artifacts; changing them alters artifact content and breaks validation.

Package paths are hashed into every freeze manifest. Renaming them would invalidate all existing manifests and require a full re-freeze and re-verification. Deferred as a separate, deliberately scoped change.
These record what was decided and what was received, at the time. Rewriting them retroactively would falsify the record.
Each is checksum-governed by PROJECT_MANIFEST.json / ORIGINALS_MANIFEST.json. Renaming files would break those manifests. They remain under their historical names.
Roughly ninety sbatch scripts hard-code it and checksummed records reference it. Renaming breaks both for no scientific gain. The pipeline README notes that the path retains its historical name.

author_signoff.note: A rename changes no claim, no number and no endpoint. It is recorded here for continuity rather than as a pre-registration amendment.

verification: Full test suite green after the rename (53 tests). Seed guards asserted: configs/confirmation_expansion.json 1, champhla_confirmation/cli.py 1, cohorts/frozen_initial_rosters.tsv 308, cohorts/frozen_initial_rosters.json 1 -- all unchanged.
